top.title: Warriors Player Ratings: Curry Drops An Efficient 25 To Blow Out Pelicans In Lopsided Matchup
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The Golden State Warriors delivered an absolute demolition of the New Orleans Pelicans , cruising to a 138-87 victory behind an explosive offensive performance. Stephen Curry finished with 25 points on efficient shooting (6-10), but he wasn’t even the Warriors’ leading scorer in a game where the entire rotation was scorching hot. Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski each scored 25 points, combining for 19-29 shooting from the field. Lendeborg was particularly impressive, knocking down all four of his three-point attempts while contributing seven rebounds and four assists. Podziemski matched the scoring total with five triples of his own. Golden State shot an incredible 54.9% from the field and 47.7% from three-point range, compared to New Orleans’ miserable 36.3% and 28.6%, respectively. The Warriors also dominated the glass 50-31, dished out 37 assists, and finished with a staggering 51-point largest lead. Here are the Warriors’ player ratings from the blowout victory. Stephen Curry: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 5 REB, 2 AST, 1 TOV, 6-10 FG, 4-7 3-PT FG, 9-9 FT, 21 MIN Curry was incredibly efficient, scoring 25 points in just 21 minutes while shooting 60.0% from the field and making four three-pointers. He also converted all nine free throws, barely wasting a scoring opportunity. The Warriors didn’t need Curry to play extended minutes, and the superstar made the most of his time on the floor. An efficient scoring performance with minimal turnovers is exactly what Golden State wants from its leader. Yaxel Lendeborg: A+ Game Stats: 23 PTS, 7 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 2 TOV, 8-10 FG, 4-4 3-PT FG, 3-4 FT, 27 MIN Lendeborg was spectacular. He finished with 23 points on just 10 shot attempts, including a perfect 4-4 performance from beyond the arc. His efficiency was remarkable, and he contributed seven rebounds and four assists along the way. Golden State received a tremendous two-way performance from Lendeborg, who finished with a team-high +34. This was precisely the kind of performance that makes a blowout even more convincing. Brandin Podziemski: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 2 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK, 10-19 FG, 5-11 3-PT FG, 26 MIN Podziemski matched Curry’s scoring total while taking on a larger offensive workload. His five three-pointers helped Golden State completely overwhelm New Orleans from the perimeter. Although he wasn’t quite as efficient as Lendeborg, Podziemski’s 25 points and four assists were instrumental in the offensive explosion. Zero turnovers made his performance even better. Al Horford: A- Game Stats: 5 PTS, 2 REB, 6 AST, 2 STL, 3 BLK, 2-5 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 15 MIN Horford was outstanding defensively and as a facilitator. Six assists, two steals, and three blocks in only 15 minutes represent an impressive all-around contribution. He also knocked down a three-pointer, helping maintain Golden State’s offensive spacing. Horford’s versatility was on full display in this dominant performance. Charles Basse

top.title: Oluwo seeks Yoruba language as medium for teaching science
top.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Oluwo of Iwo, Oba Abdulrosheed Akanbi, has called for the development and promotion of Yoruba language as a medium of instruction for academic subjects, including Physics and other specialised courses. The monarch made the call on Monday during the 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration and his 11th coronation anniversary at his palace in Iwo, Osun State. Oba Akanbi said Yoruba had the capacity to serve as a language of instruction across different academic disciplines if deliberate efforts were made to develop and expand its use. “Normally, I prefer to speak my Yoruba language. I want to upgrade the Yoruba language so that we can use it to teach Physics and all kinds of subjects and courses in the educational system,” he said. The traditional ruler also advocated the preservation and modernisation of Yoruba culture, particularly the reform of traditions he said promoted violence. While praising the richness of Yoruba heritage, he stressed the need to preserve its positive aspects while addressing practices that could encourage violence. “When it comes to culture, I want a culture that is free of violence. I accept all Yoruba cultures and traditions, but those that need modifications, particularly traditions that promote violence, must be addressed. “It is not that I totally reject them, but I understand that change takes time,” he said. The monarch also announced a N5 million empowerment scheme for at least 100 residents of Iwo, with each beneficiary expected to receive N50,000. He said the beneficiaries would be drawn from different segments of the community, including members of the royal institution, princes, chiefs, the Muslim community, traditional initiates and ordinary residents. According to him, beneficiaries will be selected randomly rather than through a predetermined process. The 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration also attracted members of different religious groups to the palace, where they offered prayers and praises to God for the monarch, his subjects, Iwo town and the country. Garry, meanwhile, is coming off a defeat to Islam Makhachev in the main event of UFC 330 , where he challenged for the welterweight championship. top.title: Mets post a meme reaction after Carson Benge missed out on NL ROY honor
top.description: David Frerker-Imagn Images Mets post a meme reaction after Carson Benge missed out on NL ROY honor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New York Mets outfielder Carson Benge came up short as Sal Stewart won NL Rookie of the Year. Benge finished with seven first-place votes and 107 points, a distant second to Stewart’s 170. The Cardinals’ JJ Wetherholt went third with 99 points. In response to Benge’s tough loss, the Mets’ official X account posted the “sitting wolf meme” with a Mets cap placed on its head. pic.twitter.com/jqtPnmiKVy Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — New York Mets (@Mets) November 10, 2026 The meme is often used to depict solitude and loneliness, which some Mets fans may be feeling after Benge missed out on the award. The Mets rookie was one of the few bright spots in another disappointing season that finished 74-88. Benge hit .282 with 20 home runs (third on the team behind Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor) and 65 RBIs. He also broke Pete Alonso’s Mets rookie record for most hits , finishing the season with a team-leading 168. Of the three Rookie of the Year finalists, Stewart, Benge, and Wetherholt, Benge was perhaps the most well-rounded option. Aside from being solid with the bat, he was also a plus on baserunning and defense, which were big knocks on Stewart. Moreover, Benge finished a close second to Wetherholt in FanGraphs WAR (4.3 to 4.6) among rookies, while Stewart was well behind at 2.0. There are several unknowns facing the Mets this offseason, one of them being Francisco Lindor’s future. But one thing that is clear is that Carson Benge is one of the team’s centerpieces moving forward. With him and Juan Soto in the outfield, the Mets should have a solid foundation to build upon for the next few years. top.title: Nixa soccer gets revenge over bogey team Glendale in district championship
top.description: SPRINGFIELD — Revenge is a dish best served cold. On a chilly evening, Nixa soccer bested Glendale 1-0 behind a late goal to lift the Class 4 district championship on Monday, Nov. 9. This was Nixa’s first victory over Glendale since 2023, after losing five straight games. It’s a moment that many of the seniors have been dreaming of, especially goalkeeper Jackson Smith. “It feels great, senior year, we haven’t beat them since freshman year,” Smith said. “For us to come out and win a district championship, it feels good for our city, our team. I’m thrilled.” Smith had a stellar game, but when a hero was needed, Gavin Shaw rose to the occasion. Cross country: Gloria Deo's Caroline Fields wins Class 1 state title with sister by her side With three minutes remaining, Shaw received the ball on the left wing. The senior danced on the ball a few times, juking out Glendale’s defense. He drove towards the byline before firing a cross. The ball ricocheted off of a Glendale defender and snuck through the goal at the near post. “It’s definitely a top momentum of my life,” Shaw said. “Scoring a game-winner in the district championship is always fun. Run to the corner and have everyone jump in and celebrate, it was super exciting.” It wasn’t the prettiest goal, but it was a testament to Nixa’s style of play. The Eagles wanted the ball down the wings and it’s where they made the most of their chances. Nixa fired cross after cross into Glendale’s box throughout the match. The variety of crosses made it difficult for Glendale. They were sometimes pinged to the six-yard line, or they were lofted to the back post. Each cross proved that Nixa was getting closer to a goal, finally hitting the back of the net with minutes to spare. “We moved our wings up the field. We wanted to make sure we’re defensively solid, but then get up and attack,” Nixa head coach Evan Palmer said. “It puts Gavin and Spencer (Rinne), who play the wing a lot, up there where they can do their stuff because they’re fantastic on the ball.” High school football: Breaking down Springfield area district semifinal action Shaw’s goal was the difference maker. The celebrations wouldn't happen without Smith’s strong wrists. He was called into action on multiple occasions, showcasing his reflexes and stopping ability. Glendale attacked down Nixa’s left wing with 10 minutes to play. A shot was fired and Shaw needed to fully extend himself to cover the back post. It was a fantastic save, but the ball filtered to the top of the box. Glendale’s next shot rattled the bar before Nixa could clear the lines. It was one of the Falcons’ best chances of the game. “I couldn’t even tell you,” Shaw said, reliving the close call. “I freaked out. I was happy, but I tried not to get too happy. I try to stay consistent and stay in the zone, but it’s hard not to get excited.” Glendale has been Nixa’s bogey team for years. In the regular season, the Falcons won 3-2. In the district championship, Nixa got its moment to shine.

top.title: Missouri requested formal SEC review into officiating after getting hosed vs. Texas
top.description: John David Mercer-USA TODAY Sports. Missouri requested formal SEC review into officiating after getting hosed vs. Texas appeared first on ClutchPoints . Missouri has formally requested the Southeastern Conference to examine the officiating from Saturday’s controversial 34-20 loss to Texas , with athletic director Laird Veatch calling for greater accountability and transparency. Veatch announced the request in a letter to Tigers fans on Monday, acknowledging the frustration surrounding several decisions that went against Missouri . “After the game Saturday, we requested a formal review and response from the SEC regarding the officiating,” shared Veatch. “Consistent with SEC expectations, we will not make those conversations or responses public, other than that we have not received anything inconsistent with what the conference has already shared publicly.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The most disputed incident occurred in the third quarter when Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning appeared to throw an incomplete pass, but officials ruled it a fumble. The replay booth upheld the original decision, giving Texas a crucial first down. The Longhorns capitalized on that possession, scoring a game-tying touchdown three plays later before adding two more touchdowns in the second half to secure the win. Other controversial decisions included a pass interference penalty against cornerback Sione Laulea, a missed intentional grounding call on Manning and the officials overturning an early rushing touchdown by Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons. Disagreements also emerged over how downfield blocking was handled on plays behind the line of scrimmage. The defeat dropped Missouri to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in conference play, knocking the Tigers out of the AP Top 25 and potentially ending their College Football Playoff hopes. Meanwhile, Texas improved its postseason position by avoiding a third loss. Missouri will next travel to Georgia before hosting Kentucky and Oklahoma in its remaining home games. top.title: Lazy Canucks Bullied By Tocchet Hockey in Tough Loss to Flyers
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Canucks looked lazy and disinterested for 40 minutes on Monday, as Philadelphia got a much-needed win at Rogers Arena by a score of 3-1. That was a classic game of Tocchet hockey. A lot of dump-ins and board battles in a very low-event game. The Canucks lost most of those board battles, which resulted in an embarrassingly low number of scoring chances, especially in the first two periods. If there was still doubt, there is no denying it now: the Canucks are the worst NHL team by a country mile. Remember, the Canucks were facing a struggling Philadelphia team that played against the Calgary Flames last night. In the end, Philadelphia bullied the Canucks and took their lunch money, and did not even need a great effort to do it. Game Stories: Chytil and Willander Out Again, Lekkerimäki Promoted, Sportsnet+ Exclusive Game As we discussed in Monday morning’s Canucks Rundown , Filip Chytil and Tom Willander were present at morning skate, but did not play tonight. Jonathan Lekkerimäki , who has had a great start this season, was rewarded with a spot on the top line with Elias Pettersson and Brock Boeser . Jacob Quillan remained a healthy scratch in this game, which remains a head-scratcher, given his heavy style of play. His forechecking, speed, and play along the wall could have been some help this game, considering how Philadelphia plays. This was the first of nine games this season where Canucks fans could only stream the game exclusively on Sportsnet+. A controversial move by Rogers as they try to drive up subscriptions. However, Canucks fans should frankly be thanking Rogers for preventing them from watching this game. This was a very tough watch. Canucks Offense Stifled in the First Period Two minutes in, Michael Bunting attempted a pass to Christian Dvorak , but the puck got between Brendan Gallagher ‘s feet and bounced to Dvorak; then Bunting found the loose puck to open the scoring. top.title: Latest Puka Nacua injury update shows WR will miss significant time for LA Rams
top.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images Puka Nacua has avoided a ligament tear after latest knee injury, but the injury update is still not good for the Los Angeles Rams. Wide receiver Puka Nacua has been great to start the year for the Los Angeles Rams, recording 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games. The star had arguably his best game of the year against the Washington Commanders, going off for 150 yards and a touchdown. However, things are never straightforward in the world of football. Nacua suffered an injury on the final offensive play against the Commanders. In a game the Rams won 20-13, the price they paid was their star receiver’s health. And while the initial fears have proven to be overblown, his injury is still significant. Puka Nacua will go on to IR, after spraining ACL and PCL and suffering turf toe When Puka went down, fans feared the worst. There was discussion about whether it would be a season-ending injury, with some speculating that Nacua had torn his ligament. The team has now assessed the situation, and it is not quite that bad. On Monday, Adam Schefter revealed the details of Nacua’s ailments, and despite the slight cause for optimism, it still isn’t what Rams fans will want to hear. “Rams WR Puka Nacua is likely to be placed injured reserve due to MCL and PCL sprains, per HC Sean McVay,” the NFL insider shared on Monday evening. This means that he is likely to miss at least a month of action, and it could be more as well. nigeria.title: Oluwo seeks Yoruba language as medium for teaching science
nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Oluwo of Iwo, Oba Abdulrosheed Akanbi, has called for the development and promotion of Yoruba language as a medium of instruction for academic subjects, including Physics and other specialised courses. The monarch made the call on Monday during the 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration and his 11th coronation anniversary at his palace in Iwo, Osun State. Oba Akanbi said Yoruba had the capacity to serve as a language of instruction across different academic disciplines if deliberate efforts were made to develop and expand its use. “Normally, I prefer to speak my Yoruba language. I want to upgrade the Yoruba language so that we can use it to teach Physics and all kinds of subjects and courses in the educational system,” he said. The traditional ruler also advocated the preservation and modernisation of Yoruba culture, particularly the reform of traditions he said promoted violence. While praising the richness of Yoruba heritage, he stressed the need to preserve its positive aspects while addressing practices that could encourage violence. “When it comes to culture, I want a culture that is free of violence. I accept all Yoruba cultures and traditions, but those that need modifications, particularly traditions that promote violence, must be addressed. “It is not that I totally reject them, but I understand that change takes time,” he said. The monarch also announced a N5 million empowerment scheme for at least 100 residents of Iwo, with each beneficiary expected to receive N50,000. He said the beneficiaries would be drawn from different segments of the community, including members of the royal institution, princes, chiefs, the Muslim community, traditional initiates and ordinary residents. According to him, beneficiaries will be selected randomly rather than through a predetermined process. The 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration also attracted members of different religious groups to the palace, where they offered prayers and praises to God for the monarch, his subjects, Iwo town and the country. nigeria.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States will hold talks in Abu Dhabi Tuesday on ending Europe’s worst conflict since World War II in the first such meeting in more than nine months, as another winter of war approaches. Europe – alarmed by US President Donald Trump floating a deal with Moscow on European security ahead of the talks – will also send representatives to Abu Dhabi. Trump has pushed for an end to the Russia-Ukraine war since returning to power, but previous talks produced no breakthroughs and the process became sidelined by the US-Israeli war against Iran. Europe and Ukraine fear the United States will force a deal on Kyiv that would amount to a de-facto capitulation, with Trump appearing to pivot towards Moscow this year. Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and has dragged on for 56 months, with the Kremlin showing no sign of backing down. Trump hinted Ukraine will have to give up land ahead of the talks, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine.” Russia occupies large swathes of Ukraine but, while its troops have grinded westwards, they have not been able to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the region it still controls, vowing it will otherwise press on with its offensive. Ukraine – which for more than 4.5 years has resisted a far larger invading army at a huge human cost – has ruled out such a withdrawal. Russia pummelled Ukraine in the run-up to the talks and carried out one of its deadliest strikes yet – with Kyiv saying 55 people were killed in a frontline village as they queued for humanitarian aid. Russia’s Vladimir Putin, who launched the war in February 2022, has repeatedly refused broader ceasefire offers and face-to-face talks with Zelensky. nigeria.title: Explainer: Election results collation chain that decides Nigeria’s president
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Nigeria’s president is not declared on the strength of a single national count. A chain of collation officers, each signing for the votes below them, builds the result from the polling unit up to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president The chain starts when voting ends. Voters are accredited with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, and the presiding officer counts the ballots in public and enters each party’s score on Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet. The presiding officer signs the form, and polling agents who are present countersign it. A poster version, Form EC60E, is pasted at the polling unit so voters can see what was recorded. Collation then moves upward. INEC’s then chairman, Mahmood Yakubu, described the 2023 process as running through “four levels”: ward, local government area, LGA, state and national. At each level, an officer adds up the forms from the level below and records the total on a new form. The election results forms The ward collation officer adds up the Form EC8A sheets in the ward and records the total on Form EC8B. The LGA collation officer then adds up the ward sheets on Form EC8C. At state level, the State Collation Officer for the Presidential Election (SCOPE) adds up the LGA results on Form EC8D. Katsina in 2023 shows what that form contains: 3,516,719 registered voters; 1,097,663 accredited; 1,058,673 valid votes, and 32,514 rejected. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, led with 489,045 votes against 482,283 for Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The national stage takes place in Abuja, with the INEC Chairman acting as returning officer for the presidential election. That office is now held by Joash Amupitan, who succeeded Yakubu in October 2025. In 2023, Yakubu set out the procedure at the national collation centre, where each state’s SCOPE presents the original Form EC8D. “When all the SCOPES have presented their results,” the returning officer displays the sealed copies of Form EC8DA, the state-by-state summary, and Form EC8E, the declaration sheet. Polling agents are invited to comment before the winner is declared, and each agent receives duplicate copies afterwards. Declaring winner Declaring the winner involves more than adding up votes. The returning officer must also confirm that the candidate with the highest total reached one-quarter of the votes in enough states, as Section 134 of the Constitution requires. The 2023 totals show the arithmetic. Yakubu put registered voters at 93,469,008; accredited voters at 25,286,616; valid votes at 24,025,940, and rejected votes at 939,278. nigeria.description: By Udeme Akpan, Ediri Ejoh, Obas Esiedesa & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s electricity generation rose to 4,020.41 megawatts (MW) on Monday from 3,500MW, but the increase has yet to translate into adequate supply for consumers across the country. This comes as the promise last Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to restore normalcy in power supply within 72 hours expired two days ago. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 20 power plants were connected to the national grid as of 1.0pm yesterday, producing a combined 4,020.41MW. The output was below Sunday’s peak generation of 4,253.6MW but above the off-peak figure of 3,862.17MW. Last Thursday, generation had dropped to 3,659MW from 3,996MW recorded the previous day, worsening supply conditions across several parts of the country. Promising restoration within 72 hours, the Ministry of Power had ruled out a major or systemic national grid failure, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges across parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. An analysis of Monday’s generation profile showed that Afam VI contributed the highest output of 519MW, followed by Shiroro Hydro Power Plant with 445MW and Azura-Edo Independent Power Plant with 438MW. Egbin Power Plant, with an installed capacity of 1,320MW, contributed 108MW. Meanwhile, load allocation to the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) stood at a combined 3,195MW as of 5:07pm yesterday; Abuja DisCo received 581MW; Ikeja 467MW; Eko 458MW and Ibadan 359MW. Others were Port Harcourt, 294MW; Benin, 243MW; Enugu, 233MW; Kano, 173MW; Kaduna, 167MW; Jos, 146MW; and Yola, 74MW. In his update on the power situation, Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said electricity had been restored to many communities affected by recent disruptions, particularly in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330kV transmission line had been repaired and returned to service, helping to raise electricity supply to the Lagos Complex to more than 1,000MW. nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1,608,660 invalid voter registrations from the preliminary voters register and identified 54 staff members across 10 states for disciplinary action, including possible prosecution, over their alleged involvement in registration irregularities. nigeria.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages. The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia. According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future. The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services. It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development. Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers. “Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need. “That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth. “We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said. Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program. The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities. It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026. The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026. The transition to a permanent programme is expected to provide rural employers with a more reliable supply of skilled foreign workers while supporting the long-term economic development of participating communities. nigeria.title: The Architecture of Becoming
nigeria.description: A Review of Tomileye E. Abolaji’s The Things Life Taught My Heart By Femi Morgan Published by i2X Media , 2026 Number of pages: 62 pages There is a moment in Tomileye E. Abolaji’s debut collection that captures the entire book of poetry. The book shows that the poet persona is lost in a new city, following the blue dot on her phone, and finds herself travelling fifteen minutes in the wrong direction. “I had not found my way,” she writes. “I had simply travelled farther from it.” It is a simple observation, almost throwaway, yet it contains the essential grammar of this book: the recognition that getting lost is not the same as being defeated, that the wrong road can still teach you something about the right one. It also hints that technology cannot replace intuition. The Things Life Taught My Heart , subtitled Twenty journeys through love, betrayal, courage, discovery and the beautiful art of BECOMING , is a collection of twenty prose poems that trace a life from its difficult beginnings to its hard-won flourishing. Abolaji, a legal counsel and performance poet who has performed in Nigeria and the UK, writes with the precision of someone trained to weigh evidence and the tenderness of someone who has learned that not all truths can be proven in a courtroom. The collection is structured into five movements, “The Wounds We Carry,” “The Things Love Leaves Behind,” “The Value of Being Seen,” “Learning to Stand,” and “Becoming More.” This architecture gives the book a satisfying arc and extends the metaphor of the collection to its structure. We begin in hurt and end in hope, but the journey is never simplistic. Abolaji understands that healing is not linear, that the wounds we carry do not disappear simply because we have learned to name them. The opening piece, “The Courage Hidden in a No,” sets the tone. A friendship dissolves when the speaker refuses a loan the poet persona cannot afford to give. The refusal is met not with understanding but with recrimination: “I became stingy, unfriendly, a terrible person in stories I had never been invited to hear.” What makes this poem remarkable is its refusal to apologise for the boundary drawn. “Kindness should never require the destruction of one’s peace,” Abolaji writes, and the line lands with the force of a verdict. The poem ends with a question that is really a declaration: “if my no makes me a stranger in a friendship that only understands yes, perhaps I have not lost as much as I once feared.” This is a book about learning to trust one’s own judgment, and Abolaji returns to this theme repeatedly. nigeria.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors. Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors. According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state. He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.” Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters. He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration. Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions. He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates. The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration. “That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said. Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The Golden State Warriors delivered an absolute demolition of the New Orleans Pelicans , cruising to a 138-87 victory behind an explosive offensive performance. Podziemski matched the scoring total with five triples of his own. Golden State shot an incredible 54.9% from the field and 47.7% from three-point range, compared to New Orleans’ miserable 36.3% and 28.6%, respectively. The Warriors also dominated the glass 50-31, dished out 37 assists, and finished with a staggering 51-point largest lead. Here are the Warriors’ player ratings from the blowout victory. Stephen Curry: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 5 REB, 2 AST, 1 TOV, 6-10 FG, 4-7 3-PT FG, 9-9 FT, 21 MIN Curry was incredibly efficient, scoring 25 points in just 21 minutes while shooting 60.0% from the field and making four three-pointers. He also converted all nine free throws, barely wasting a scoring opportunity. The Warriors didn’t need Curry to play extended minutes, and the superstar made the most of his time on the floor. An efficient scoring performance with minimal turnovers is exactly what Golden State wants from its leader. Yaxel Lendeborg: A+ Game Stats: 23 PTS, 7 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 2 TOV, 8-10 FG, 4-4 3-PT FG, 3-4 FT, 27 MIN Lendeborg was spectacular. sports.title: Nixa soccer gets revenge over bogey team Glendale in district championship
sports.description: SPRINGFIELD — Revenge is a dish best served cold. On a chilly evening, Nixa soccer bested Glendale 1-0 behind a late goal to lift the Class 4 district championship on Monday, Nov. 9. This was Nixa’s first victory over Glendale since 2023, after losing five straight games. It’s a moment that many of the seniors have been dreaming of, especially goalkeeper Jackson Smith. “It feels great, senior year, we haven’t beat them since freshman year,” Smith said. “For us to come out and win a district championship, it feels good for our city, our team. I’m thrilled.” Smith had a stellar game, but when a hero was needed, Gavin Shaw rose to the occasion. Cross country: Gloria Deo's Caroline Fields wins Class 1 state title with sister by her side With three minutes remaining, Shaw received the ball on the left wing. The senior danced on the ball a few times, juking out Glendale’s defense. He drove towards the byline before firing a cross. The ball ricocheted off of a Glendale defender and snuck through the goal at the near post. “It’s definitely a top momentum of my life,” Shaw said. “Scoring a game-winner in the district championship is always fun. Run to the corner and have everyone jump in and celebrate, it was super exciting.” It wasn’t the prettiest goal, but it was a testament to Nixa’s style of play. The Eagles wanted the ball down the wings and it’s where they made the most of their chances. Nixa fired cross after cross into Glendale’s box throughout the match. The variety of crosses made it difficult for Glendale. They were sometimes pinged to the six-yard line, or they were lofted to the back post. Each cross proved that Nixa was getting closer to a goal, finally hitting the back of the net with minutes to spare. “We moved our wings up the field. We wanted to make sure we’re defensively solid, but then get up and attack,” Nixa head coach Evan Palmer said. “It puts Gavin and Spencer (Rinne), who play the wing a lot, up there where they can do their stuff because they’re fantastic on the ball.” High school football: Breaking down Springfield area district semifinal action Shaw’s goal was the difference maker. The celebrations wouldn't happen without Smith’s strong wrists. He was called into action on multiple occasions, showcasing his reflexes and stopping ability. Glendale attacked down Nixa’s left wing with 10 minutes to play. A shot was fired and Shaw needed to fully extend himself to cover the back post. It was a fantastic save, but the ball filtered to the top of the box. Glendale’s next shot rattled the bar before Nixa could clear the lines. It was one of the Falcons’ best chances of the game. “I couldn’t even tell you,” Shaw said, reliving the close call. “I freaked out. I was happy, but I tried not to get too happy. I try to stay consistent and stay in the zone, but it’s hard not to get excited.” Glendale has been Nixa’s bogey team for years. In the regular season, the Falcons won 3-2. In the district championship, Nixa got its moment to shine.

technology.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
technology.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. The product has become particularly useful since Anthropic's Mythos model, and similar AI offerings, made it possible to quickly find more software bugs and flaws and overwhelmed tech teams whose patching apparatus was not set up to handle hundreds of montly CVEs. Live Protect currently works on some of Cisco's datacenter switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. "Expect this to be a major investment area," Schultz added. ®

He said the tool is now “super-charged by Mythos” and will identify more danger that AI Defense will then address. AI Defense already uses AI-powered red teaming to find flaws. Mythos will become another option. Cisco will make it available under users’ existing licenses, without additional cost. Natalie Mead, Anthropic’s head of applied AI for the Asia-Pacific, said the company has a long queue of buyers who want to use Mythos, and working with Cisco will make it easier to satisfy that demand. Anthropic initially made Mythos available under "Project Glasswing," a program that gave vetted organizations access to the model to test their codebases, but has since expanded access through other controlled programs, an arrangement that makes considerable sense because in the wrong hands Mythos could help attackers exploit software flaws. The Cisco deal exposes the functionality of Mythos to end-users, without letting them use the model itself. The Register asked Mead if Anthropic has similar deals with other third parties and she demurred. That may be because a few hours after Cisco told us about its use of Mythos, IBM announced that it will also integrate Anthropic’s model into a product – namely its Concert tool, which uses AI to scan applications for risks and weaknesses. IBM says it will use Mythos “to uncover weaknesses traditional scanners miss, determine which pose real risk and generate fixes for developer approval.” We have asked Anthropic if these integrations represent a decision to open Mythos to more users in more ways. We will update this story if we receive a substantial response. Also on Monday, Anthropic introduced version 5.2 of Mythos and Fable, which the company says generate outputs up to 30 percent faster than version 5.1 yet cost less: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. It's unclear whether the pair chose to resign or were forced out, or what will happen to their planned slate of projects beyond 2028's Superman: Man of Tomorrow , which is in post-production. Producer Jeremy Latcham—a protege of Marvel's Kevin Feige who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy among other MCU films—will replace them. Per Gunn and Safran's joint statement : Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker , Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow . DCU fans are mourning the news and what it could mean for the franchise. My feelings are mixed. On the one hand, I'm on record that I’ve found the rebooted DC Universe films released thus far to be enjoyable but rather forgettable, even when the positives outweigh the negatives . But HBO has done right by the DCU: I loved both seasons of Peacemaker; Lanterns is a shining beacon of what is possible when someone is allowed to get really creative within the genre; and I'm very much looking forward to next year's Jimmy Olsen (Skylar Gisondo) series The People v. science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Roger C. Wiens, SuperCam Principal Investigator for NASA’s Perseverance rover at Purdue University Nov. 4, 2026 Exploration on Mars turns up the unexpected. Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of elements. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. The results were published in Geophysical Research Letters by a team led by Ann Ollila earlier this year, so you can read all about it. The gemstone version of chromium-containing corundum is ruby. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. While we haven’t found collectable rubies on Mars yet, the little corundum crystals are helping us learn more about Mars’ past. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. However, large meteor and asteroid impacts can create local metamorphism due to long-term heating from the impact. Because we are in a very ancient terrain near the rim of Jezero crater, we can expect some evidence of localized metamorphism. As the first mission in such terrain, we are learning new things. As previously reported , that rock had a hardness too high to core. However, the team felt strongly that it was worth the effort to add a gabbro, an igneous rock made mostly of calcium-rich plagioclase feldspar and pyroxene crystals, to Perseverance’s sample collection . In search of a new local gabbroic candidate to sample, Perseverance traveled about 100 meters (330 feet) to a different patch of light-toned rocks . Indeed, visual and chemical data from the light-toned rocks in the new workspace revealed a composition similar to that of “Badger Peak.” NASA’s Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image of the abrasion patch “Pumbe” using its SHERLOC WATSON camera, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm. The image was acquired on Oct. 17, 2026 (Sol 2011), at a local mean solar time of 16:14:35. The abrasion patch is about 5 centimeters (2 inches) across. NASA/JPL-Caltech To improve the odds of collecting a sample this time, the team made prudent decisions: choosing a neighboring rock with a flatter surface better oriented for the drill stabilizers to press against, and using a coring bit with less wear. At last, in a display of the rover’s namesake quality, the drill made it about 3.1 centimeters (1.2 inches) into the rock. Sample acquisition activities followed, making “Singita” the rover’s first sample in more than a year. While Singita is the newest sample, it may be among the oldest rocks in Perseverance’s collection . Textures in the rock suggest that it likely formed deep in the crust and was modified and excavated by at least one, and possibly multiple, large impact events. Perseverance has now completed its 66 th successful abrasion and collected an intriguing new sample alongside it. science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos “It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun , director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time . The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. A view of the Apollo 4 launch after stage separation looking back down at Earth from the Saturn V rocket. NASA/Interm Archives/Getty The uncrewed Apollo 4 command module splashes down under parachutes after a smooth test flight. NASA/Interm Archives/Getty “The maiden voyage of the Saturn V dramatically increased the confidence of people across the nation in the management of the largest research and development undertaking in which the western world has ever engaged,” George Mueller, NASA's then-Associate Administrator for Manned Space Flight, said at the time . science.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029 , when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo . Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. science.title: NYT bestseller ‘Robopocalypse’ is getting a TV series with Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman at the helm
science.description: null They say all good things come to those who wait… and WAIT. Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. It does seem like an eternity since news first broke that Portland-based New York Times bestselling author Daniel H. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay. That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required. But now we have been blessed with the news , first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. And what timing, just as AI fever has gripped the planet with paranoia centered around our eventual robot overlords. "'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and suspense of a major action story, but what drew me to it are the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its center," Ron Howard shared in a statement. As a PhD graduate of Carnegie Mellon University’s Robotics Institute and a future king of the techno-thriller, Wilson was the ideal writer to bring this frightening story to life, and a 2014 sequel titled "Robogenesis" was equally gripping. science.title: NASA’s Chandra Finds Source of Star’s Mysterious Outbursts
science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. The luminous blue variable and supernova impostor AT 2016blu is in the middle of the small square. X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. However, unlike in a supernova explosion, the star is not destroyed, so AT 2016blu is also referred to as a “supernova impostor.” Between 2012 and 2026, astronomers detected at least 27 bursts of optical light, or light in wavelengths that are visible to our eyes, from AT 2016blu roughly every 113 days. “This star’s behavior was confusing at first because it kept acting like a supernova, but clearly it’s not because it keeps surviving these outbursts about three times a year,” said co-author Núria Torres-Albà, also of the University of Virginia. “To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized we needed X-ray data, timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst.” The team used Chandra because it is the only X-ray telescope with sharp enough vision to distinguish AT 2016blu

science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said. science.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
science.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them." Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event . Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd. The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group. But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them. "The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved." "We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night . We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base. NASA Adminisrator Jared Isaacman invites students to help NASA build a moon base at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd) How will it work? This challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the U.S. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety . This will be what Isaacman described as a "multi-phase competition that mirrors how ideas are developed actually in the aerospace industry." science.title: Netflix announces 'Stranger Things' spin-off 'Other Worlds', and it's already teasing a trip to Area 51 (video)
science.description: null So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 . The teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any TV show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Of course, the tease doesn't end there, as the thunder booms in the sky and there's a visual hint of a wormhole. No story details about "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" have been released to date, but there are some clues out there for all the Internet sleuths. Trefrey wrote the Henry Creel-focused "Stranger Things: The First Shadow" play, while Matt Duffer explained to Variety how a spin-off show would tackle the rock that Henry found in the briefcase in "Stranger Things." So, yes, expect this to be a Henry-centric affair and the start of his long, hard road to hell and becoming Vecna. (Image credit: Netflix) What'll be interesting, though, is to see how the show ties into the history of Area 51. After all, it was on April 12, 1955, that CIA officer Richard Bissell discovered the site, while the "Other Worlds" trailer has the date of April 19th clearly marked onscreen, so the timelines align nicely here. "Stranger Things" has never been shy of tying itself to real-world science and historical events, so it'll be fascinating to see how the show explores Area 51 as a concept and the secrets everybody believes are hidden there. Was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was E.T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? Who knows, with all this renewed excitement around this mysterious military facility, we might get another "Storm Area 51" event to enjoy and laugh at all over again. Regardless, more "Stranger Things" is welcome news, and since it's presumably about one of the show's best characters, Henry Creel, it only adds another layer to his already intriguing lore. If we can't have an origin story about Hopper's incredible and envious moustache, this is the next best thing. "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" arrives on Netflix in 2028.
